newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak SAX dips further on Slovnaft share losses.
newsitem.headline: Slovak SAX dips further on Slovnaft share losses.

text.p: Leading Slovak blue chips closed mixed in listless trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Wednesday, with the SAX index dipping 0.56 points to 180.46 on losses to shares of oil refiner Slovnaft.
Slovnaft lost 12 crowns to close at 738, with brokers saying its decline may be the result of the overall bearish sentiment on the market.

"You find offers to sell the stock for a price of less than 800 crowns, but there is no interest in Slovnaft shares, which is probably caused by the mood on the market," said Dusan Sykora of ING Barings.
Steel producer VSZ closed 10 crowns lower at 560. Brokers have said the shares share as overvalued, and its real price may be at some 530 crowns.
The largest commercial bank VUB was the only blue chip to post slight gains, closing up 25 crowns at 1,690.
Oil and gas storage firm Nafta did not trade.
"There is seems to be no sign of revival of the market in the next few weeks, the future is as black as the night outside," Sykora said.
Overall volume rose to 1,227,880 shares, boosted by direct trades, from 625,007 stocks traded on Wednesday.
The turnover increased to 429.59 million crowns, from 245.02 million on Wednesday.
